canDo: Can organise a short story as “background → sudden event → outcome”.
review: Review D5–D7; focus on deciding by what the tense does, not just by time adverbs.
input: Listening: accidents/delays; reading: a short story about an accident or a trip.
output: Write 100 words about a small incident; speak for 2 minutes with at least 3 background + event pairs.
checkpoint: Can explain the reasons for 5 tense choices; both tenses appear in the story with sensible functions.
challenge: Today’s challenge: in RFI’s Journal en français facile, find a news item about an accident or mishap and retell it in 3 sentences (imparfait for the background, passé composé for the sudden event and the outcome); then use the same structure to write about a small mishap of your own.

questions.why: The imparfait « il fonctionnait normalement » describes the ongoing state the day before, showing the breakdown was sudden. Neither the weather nor how long the repairman took is evidence that it was foreseeable.
« attendait assise sur une chaise » — the imparfait gives a background action going on during the repair. The one who phoned was the narrator.
At the end she proposes putting up the emergency repair number on every floor. The circuit board has already been replaced; the chair was a stopgap on the day, not her proposal.
First a one-hour delay, meal vouchers at noon, then at 15 the departure is announced for the next day — getting steadily worse. There is no cancellation and no luggage problem in the text.
« Ce qui m'a le plus surprise, ce n'est pas le retard lui-même : c'est que personne ne savait quoi nous dire. » explicitly rules out the length of the wait itself.
Scheduled for 6 h 40, it actually left at 7 h 10 the next day — 24 and a half hours later. The twelve hours in the headline is the wait at the airport, not the total delay.
The direct cause of the braking was the van pulling out. The slippery road is the background (imparfait), and the parked cars are a long-standing problem residents raised.
« elle portait un casque et n'a pas été blessée ». The mirror hasn’t been installed yet; the driver stopping happened after the fall.
The ending only says braking distance doubles on a wet road. The other two options move the “doubling” onto things the text never mentions.
From 19 h 20 to 22 h 40, about three hours twenty minutes. One hour is the threshold they want to trigger a notification; the repair was finished that night, but the power cut didn’t last all night.
The text says câble endommagé pendant des travaux de voirie. Cooking is what residents were doing when the power went, not the cause.
One of the two demands is a text message when it lasts more than an hour. Working at night is how this repair was done, not a demand.
The driver asks passengers to get off because the road ahead is closed after an accident. The metro is the later alternative, not the reason for getting off.
She asks for the budget part to be left until last. She prepared the figures last night and has them with her.
« une bonne demi-heure de retard ». 10 h 15 is when she expects to arrive, not how late she is.
« Je lisais et je ne l'ai pas repris en sortant » — the imparfait describes what was going on then. The other two options don’t appear in the text.
« un sac gris hier soir, mais sans ordinateur » — the key is sauf.
Only une pièce d'identité is mentioned. The red label is how to identify the bag, not something to bring.
« immobilisés pendant trois heures avant que la circulation ne reprenne, vers 6 heures » — traffic had resumed by the time of the broadcast. Noon is when the orange alert ends.
The reason is that the school buses can’t run. An orange alert doesn’t in itself close schools.
Minus six is the low already reached last night (the plus-que-parfait « étaient descendues »); the rise in temperature is tomorrow.
The plus-que-parfait « je l'avais garée dans la rue le matin » shows the car had been parked elsewhere beforehand. At 18 the wind was already strong.
He sent the photos on Monday and the assessor comes on Thursday. It’s the second neighbour who hasn’t contacted the insurer yet.
The branch that hit the fence was at the first neighbour’s. The second says « on n'a rien eu, mais le portail ne ferme plus très bien ».

title: The core of narrative: two past tenses
